Remembering 9/11
The American flag is flying at half-staff today as the US recognizes the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.
The day remains the deadliest terrorist attack in modern history. In total, 2,977 people were directly killed—2,606 in the World Trade Center, 246 across four hijacked planes, and 125 at the Pentagon in Washington, DC. Tens of thousands more were injured in the aftermath or suffer from long-term illnesses caused by the debris (
read Wednesday’s write-up
The attacks were the catalyst for protracted wars in
Afghanistan
and
Iraq
. Over 7,000 US military personnel were killed, and another 53,560 were wounded across both missions. Today’s anniversary comes five years after the Taliban, which harbored al-Qaida, regained control of Afghanistan following the withdrawal of US and NATO troops in 2021. Record August Heat
August was the
joint-hottest month
ever recorded globally, tying July 2023, according to data released by the EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service. Explore the data
here
Combined global air and sea surface temperatures averaged 62.53 degrees Fahrenheit (16.96 degrees Celsius), nearly 3 degrees (1.65 C) above preindustrial levels. That exceeds the 1.5 C
warming threshold
set by the 2015 Paris climate agreement, though the target refers to long-term averages rather than a single month. Copernicus attributed the heat primarily to greenhouse gas emissions, compounded by a supersized El Niño warming the Pacific. Western Europe and the contiguous US both recorded their hottest summers, and the eight hottest months on record have all occurred since July 2023. Watch how El Niño shapes
global climate
August is typically cooler globally than July—a reversal that has occurred only four other times since 1940. See how much climate change influences daily temperatures
in your city
